doc.title: Christine Jensen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 4, 2024

title: New album of commissions compared with Habitat and Treelines
summary: She describes her forthcoming album of seven commissioned pieces and how it differs from Habitat and Treelines, reorchestrated for her Montreal ensemble.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Ooh ra. Well that’s a big album. And I’m putting a new one out in June that I’m really excited about, which is ironically about the subject we’re talking about. And I think, I highlighted in my liner notes that nobody’s going to read ‘cause they’re not going to buy the CD because they’re going to just listen to it on Spotify, no offense. But each piece has been a commission. There are seven pieces, six of them are big commissions and one actually is kind of an inner commission from my bandmates to myself, we all commissioned each other, or gave each other topics to pass around. So I don’t even have time to get into it on the liner notes because there’s not enough space anymore, unless I write a book about it, which I might have to do on the side eventually. But where was I going with this? The commissioning idea? Oh yeah, so this whole album coming up is kind of different from “Habitat” and “Treelines” because those were, for the most part, me hanging out in my space. And I suppose the commissioning came from quite a bit of government funding because I was always running off to a retreat to write or for having some reason to write. Like sometimes I was like I just want to write for my band. I want to write for the musicians that are in my band, I want to write for all sorts of things. This one is like I’ve written for a bunch of different situations like what you described. You know how much money are you paying me, who’s the soloist in the band, what are the highlights, what’s the topic? One guy was so cool, he was like, “I loved ‘Treelines’ so much but you didn’t call a song ‘Treelines.’ Can you write a piece called ‘Treelines?’” And I was like that’s brilliant, you’re right I never did write a piece called “Treelines.” So that was on “Habitat.” So it was like a little connector. And now this next one is, for the most part, commissions that may or may not have featured my sister or may have featured myself or may have featured other musicians. And then I just kind of re- orchestrated it to match the ensemble I worked with in Montreal going back to “Habitat” and “Treelines.”
